name: Amplify API
description:
This API describes the interfaces for interacting with the Outbrain Amplify product. More information about Amplify can be found on our website: http://www.outbrain.com/amplify.

At this time we are working with a select number of partners to integrate the Amplify API. To be considered for the Amplify API private beta please register for the beta plan.

If you have any questions, issues, feature requests as well as if you're interested in announcments of new features, please join our Google group:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/outbrain-amplifyapi

API Url

The base url for all API end-points is https://api.outbrain.com/amplify/v0.1/

Troubleshooting

If you're experiencing any issues or any other difficulties, please post a new topic in our Google group: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/outbrain-amplifyapi

Please attach to your post the AMPLIFY-REQUEST-ID header from the returned response. This header allows us to identify your unique request and helps us to reply quicker and more efficiently.

Updates

Aug 13, 2026

New: Brand Logo

You can now read and set a brand logo via the API. A new logoMetadata field has been added to the Marketer entity, and to the PromotedLink entity (available via extraFields=LogoMetaData) so an individual ad can carry its own logo.

Feb 1, 2026

New: Section Volume Control for CBS Campaigns

You can now provide feedback on individual section performance for your CBS Auto mode campaigns (tROAS, tCPA, Max Conversion). This allows you to increase or decrease traffic volume from specific sections based on your own external data, such as LTV or ROAS. A new volumeControl object has been added to the Campaign entity to manage these adjustments.

Jan 4, 2026

Enhanced Publisher and Section Exclusion Experience

We are introducing a new publisher and section exclusion experience that allows advertisers to apply temporary or permanent blocks, either individually or in bulk. This update provides clearer visibility, predictable behavior, and the ability to easily undo or adjust exclusions via the API.

Why This Matters

Publisher traffic can spike temporarily due to breaking news or viral events, attracting audiences that may not align with advertiser intent. During these periods, campaigns often generate clicks with few conversions, inflating costs.

Temporary exclusions allow you to pause this inventory while the news cycle is active. The system then automatically reintroduces the inventory once traffic normalizes—avoiding the need for unnecessary permanent blocks.

Technical Implementation: New expiration Field under blockedSites

To enable temporary blocking, we have added a new optional field named expiration to both the blockedPublishers and blockedSections objects under blockedSites.

Key Functionalities

  • Auto-Expiration: Temporary exclusions automatically expire and reintroduce inventory without alerts.

  • Re-activation: You can now update settings for sections that were previously Permanently blocked, overriding the original exclusion state.

  • Inheritance: Duplicated campaigns will inherit the existing exclusion states (Temporary or Permanent) of the original campaign.

Important Notes

  • Reporting: History changes will now track the distinction between permanent and temporary exclusions.

  • CSV Limitation: Exclusions uploaded via CSV files remain Permanent by default at this time (the expiration field is not yet supported in CSV uploads).

Action Required

Review your current blocking logic. If you wish to utilize temporary blocking for viral events, update your integration to populate the expiration field in your blockedPublishers and blockedSections payloads.

Oct 16, 2025

Upcoming Change to Minimum Campaign Budget Effective November 3rd 2025

To help increase campaign performance and ensure new campaigns can generate results in a timely fashion, we are adjusting the minimum required budget. This change will ensure campaigns have sufficient daily spend for our optimization systems to function effectively

Summary of the Change

  • What: The minimum daily budget for a new campaign will be increased from $20.00 to $25.00 USD.

  • Effective Date: This change will take effect on November 3rd 2025

  • Scope: This change applies only to newly created campaigns. Existing campaigns with budgets under $25.00 will continue to run without any interruption or required changes.

How This Affects You

Starting November 3rd, 2025, any API call to the POST /budgets endpoint will enforce the following rules:

  • If type = "DAILY", then amount must be greater than or equal to 25.

  • If type = "MONTHLY", then amount must be greater than or equal to 750.

  • If type = "CAMPAIGN", then amount must be greater than or equal to 25 x number of campaign days.

Additionally:

  • Any API call to the PUT /budgets endpoint to update campaigns created after November 3rd, 2025, will have the same enforcement rules outlined above.

Important Note: Daily limits for other currencies are exposed via the GET /currencies endpoint.

Action Required

Please review your budget and campaign creation and update logic and ensure that any new campaigns are created with a daily budget of at least $25.00. We recommend making this update in your integration before the effective date to ensure a smooth transition.

Jul 8, 2025

New Performance Report Endpoint - Marketers Report

You can now retrieve performance reporting aggregated by Marketers aggregation, using your primary account ID.

To obtain your primary account ID, use the Marketer Entity with the extraFields=Account param.

Dec 22, 2024

New Filter Added to reporting endpoints: enabledCampaignsOnly

You can now filter data to include only active campaigns by using the enabledCampaignsOnly field when using our reporting endpoints (promoted content, Periodic, publishers, sections etc).

  • Current Default Value: false

  • Future Default Value: true (effective end of January 2025)

Please note that while the current default value for enabledCampaignsOnly is false, it will change to true by the end of January 2025.

Sep 22, 2024

New Recommendation Field for CBS Auto modes campaigns - maxCpcRecommendation

You can now get an indication if our algo wants to bid higher than the specified "max average CPC" (or "bid cap" in old versions) on auto mode campaigns.

Similar to the data provided on Amplify dashboard, where you can see if the algorithm wants to bid higher than the specified max CPC, you can now access this indication via the API.

resourceGroups.name: Overview and Entities
resourceGroups.description:
The API is RESTful and is structured into the following core entities:

  • Marketer: A customer account.

  • Budget: A budget that contains money to be spent on one or more campaigns.

  • Campaign: A collection of promoted links.

  • PromotedLink: A single piece of promoted content.

  • PerformanceBy*: A variety of analytics entities to retrieve metrics.

The following operations may be performed via this API:

Entity Function
Marketer Read
Budget Read, Create, Update
Campaign Read, Create, Update
PromotedLink Read, Create, Update
Performance* Read

Performance* refers to the many entities that represent reporting data. For example, here are a few of our 9 different reporting endpoints:

  • Performance for a Marketer per day

  • Performance for a Campaign per day

  • Performance for a PromotedLink per day

HTTP Requests

We follow RESTful conventions of using HTTP methods to determine the type of action requested:

HTTP Method Action
GET Retrieve a resource or a list of resources
POST Create a resource.
PUT Update a resource.

When issuing a POST/PUT request that includes a json of the created/updated entitiy the following header must be included in the request:

Content-Type: application/json

HTTP Status Code Replies

HTTP Status Code Meaning Description
200 OK The request was successful.
400 Bad Request The request could not be understood or was missing required parameters
401 Unauthorized Authentication failed or user doesn't have permissions for requested operation
403 Forbidden Access denied
404 Not Found Resource was not found
429 Too Many Requests Request exceeded rate limits

Error Handling

When the API returns a status code indicating an error (400, 401, 403, 404, 429) it will also include the JSON describing the error. For example:

{
   "moreInfo" : "get-budget",
   "errorMessage" : "access denied"
}

resourceGroups.name: Authentications
resourceGroups.description:
Token

Obtaining a token should be your 1st step toward using Amplify API. You need to include it in all further requests using the HTTP Header OB-TOKEN-V1. In order to protect your privacy, the tokens are valid for a period of 30 days. You will not be able to access Amplify API using an expired token. You can generate as many tokens as you wish. Generating a new token does not invalidate older tokens. When a user password or email are changed in the Create Token Page all tokens generated prior to the change are revoked and a new token must be generated.

How to obtain a token ?

There are 2 ways to obtain a token

via web interface

Simply go to your Amplify API Token Page, fill in your password, hit generate, and you will get your token. If you can't see Amplify API Token form, this means that your username doesn't have access to the Amplify API. To register for the Amplify API please fill in this form.

actions.name: via API
actions.description:
Yes, you can obtain a new token using the Amplify API. Why? API is all about automation, so why not obtain a new token using the API before your token expires?

This API transaction is the only one in which you need to supply your Outbrain credentials.

Your credentials should be sent using Basic Authentication.

This means that the HTTP Request should include a header:

named Authorization value: BASIC BASE-64-ENC(YOUR_OUTBRAIN_USER_NAME:YOUR_OUTBRAIN_PASSWORD)

Since all communication to Amplify API are HTTPS, your credentials are safe.

You can try it using curl command (add -v to actually see the Authorization HTTP header:

curl -u YOUR_OUTBRAIN_USER_NAME:YOUR_OUTBRAIN_PASSWORD https://api.outbrain.com/amplify/v0.1/login

Transport Layer Security version 1.2 (TLS 1.2) is mandatory for communication with Amplify API. You will need to verify that your environment supports TLS 1.2, and if necessary make appropriate updates.

Please note that older versions of curl do not support TLS 1.2 and need to be upgraded.

responses.body: {"OB-TOKEN-V1":"IF_YOU_GOT_THIS_TOKEN_IT_MEANS_THAT_YOU_ARE_USING_OUR_MOCK_SERVER__USE_OUTBRAIN_PRODUCTION_SERVER_TO_GET_A_LIVE_TOKEN"}

resourceGroups.name: Rate Limits
resourceGroups.description:
The following rate limits will be enforced to different levels of the API starting November 1, 2016:

  • Authentication requests to obtain token (/login) limited to 2 requests per hour per user.

  • Usage of a single token limited to 30 requests per second for the entire API.

  • Each marketer is limited to 30 requests per minute for the entire performance reporting API (see Reports rate limits).

  • Each marketer is limited to 50 requests per minute for the entire realtime performance reporting API (see Realtime reports rate limits).

In any case of rate limit violation the response status will be 429 (Too Many Requests).

Responses with 429 status also contain HTTP Header rate-limit-msec-left, whose value marks the remaining number of milliseconds left in which the rate limit will be in effect. For exmple, if the value of rate-limit-msec-left is 35024, each request within the next 35.024 seconds will violate the rate limit and return with response status 429. Only requests issued after more than 35.024 seconds will be served.

Given the limitation on /login requests, the recommended way to manage tokens is to store an active token to be used in all requests, and periodically update it. Since each token is valid for 30 days, the update period should be 30 days or less.

resourceGroups.name: Multiple Conversions
resourceGroups.description:
Multiple Conversions gives the ability to track any of the actions a user takes after clicking through to your content. You can track everything from top of funnel (page landings and time on site) to bottom of funnel (e-book downloads and product purchases).

Please note: This new feature requires the installation of the new multiple conversion pixel which can be retrieved from your account on Outbrain.com. If you have the old conversion pixel placed you will need to remove that before installing the Multiple Conversion Pixel. If both pixels are installed there will be overcounting of data and results will be inaccurate.

resourceGroups.name: Budgets
resourceGroups.description:
Budget objects represent an amount of money to be spent via the Amplify platform. A single Budget may be shared among Campaigns (also known as a "shared budget"), though it is more common to have just one Campaign per Budget.

For convenience, Budget objects are often embedded inside the Campaign objects.

actions.name: Update an existing Budget
actions.description:
To update a Budget send a JSON with the updated value for one or more of the updatable Budget attributes.

All attribute values left unset in this PUT will remain unchanged.

Only the following Budget properties are updatable:

  • amount - The amount must be lower than the maximumAmount. A budget's minimum amount limit is determined by its type:

    DAILY - more than 25

    MONTHLY - more than 750

    CAMPAIGN - The campaign's days amount multiplied by 25

  • startDate - The start date cannot be in the past. Start date cannot be modified after budget has started (ie: start date already passed)

  • endDate - The end date must be after the start date, and cannot be in the past.

  • runForever - If set to 'true', the 'endDate' attribute should not be included as it is meaningless. The current 'endDate' attribute of the Budget (if exists) will be discarded. In case of passing 'false', 'endDate' attribute must be also passed.

  • dailyTarget - The maximum amount of spend that is allowed per day. Relevant only if DAILY_TARGET pacing is used.

  • type - Allows to move between different budget types.

  • pacing - Allows to move between different pacing types (dailyTarget paramenter have to be set when moving to DAILY_TARGET pacing).

amountRemaining Money The unspent monetary amount remaining on this Budget. read-only 150.00
amountSpent Money The spent monetary amount of this Budget. read-only 1850.00

type Budget Type Controls on which period the Budget refreshes "MONTHLY"
pacing Pacing Type Controls how fast the Budget will be spent "AUTOMATIC"
dailyTarget Money The maximum amount of spend that is allowed per day. Relevant for DAILY_TARGET pacing. 100.00
maximumAmount Money The maximum amount allowed if defined read-only 100.00

resourceGroups.name: Campaigns

Campaigns contain many PromotedLinks and define Budget, targeting, cpc, etc. Campaign settings apply to the PromotedLinks contained in a specific Campaign.

The Campaign object has the following attributes:

Property Type Semantic Example
id String campaign id. "00f4b02153ee75f3c9dc4fc128ab041962"
name String campaign name. "My Campaign"
marketerId String marketer id. "00f4b02153ee75f3c9dc4fc128ab041963"
enabled Boolean is campaign enabled. true
cpc Money cost per click. 0.58
minimumCpc Money the minimal possible cost per click. read-only 0.2
currency String The currency of the Budget amount. read-only "USD"
autoArchived Boolean Indicates whether this Campaign is archived. true
targeting Targeting Object See Targeting object.
feeds Array of RSS feeds Each feed contains the URL of the rss feed.
autoExpirationOfPromotedLinks Numeric A number specifying within how many days PromotedLinks are expired - PromotedLinks expire X days after their publication day (if known), otherwise - X days after their creation date. 7
contentType Content Type The Campaign's content type. "NATIVE_VIDEO"
budget Budget see Budget entity. read-only
suffixTrackingCode SuffixTrackingCode A parameter list that will be appended to the Campaign's PromotedLink. Use the value "EMPTY_SUFFIX" to delete. "utm_source=outb&utm_medium=cpc&utm_campaign=Celebrity-2-1"
prefixTrackingCode PrefixTrackingCode A marketer's prefix for a PromotedLink. The prefixTrackingCode must be in a valid url form and must end with some parameter followed by an equals sign. Use the value "EMPTY_PREFIX" to delete. "http://www.marketersServer.com?redirectTo="
lastModified Time The time when the Campaign was last modified. This field is affected by changes in the following properties only: name, enabled, cpc, archived read-only "2013-03-16 10:32:31"
creationTime Time The time when the Campaign was created. read-only "2013-01-18 07:19:16"
liveStatus Live Status holds Campaign's on air and spend information. read-only.
cpcPerAdEnabled Boolean Indicates whether or not the 'CPC Per Ad' feature is enabled for this campaign. If the feature has not been enabled, any CPC changes to the promoted link will not be taken into account.

trackingPixels Array of Tracking Pixels Deprecated please use pixels.trackingPixels instead (will be removed in 1.7.2021). Array of tracking pixels attached to each promoted link under this campaign
bids Bids CPC adjustments
campaignOptimization CampaignOptimization Conversion optimization settings
volumeControl Volume Control Section volume control adjustments
onAirType Campaign On Air Type Represents the scheduling type for the campaign to be on air "Scheduled"
scheduling Campaign Scheduling Rules The campaign scheduling rules
objective Campaign Objective The campaign objective

resourceGroups.name: Segments
resourceGroups.description:
Segments give the ability to segment customers based on their actions, and retarget them with new or existing campaigns. This translates into your campaigns reaching a highly engaged audience that is more likely to convert and fulfill your brand's goals. With this functionality you'll be able to segment customers in two ways: Audience Retargeting (Type: PIXEL) and Story Sequencing (Type: CLICKERS).

Please note: The PIXEL feature requires the installation of the Outbrain Custom Audience pixel, which can be retrieved from your account on Outbrain.com. If you have the old audience pixel installed, you will need to remove that before installing the new pixel. For additional information regarding obtaining and installing the pixel properly, please visit our help center here: http://help.outbrain.com/customer/en/portal/articles/2809479-how-can-i-create-custom-audiences

parameters.description: the Segment id

actions.name: Update an Existing Segment
actions.description:
To update a segment send a JSON with the updated value for one or more of the updatable segment attributes.

All attribute values left unset in this PUT will remain unchanged.

Only the following Segment properties are updatable:

  • name - Maximum length is 100 characters

  • description - Maximum length is 500 characters

  • enabled - Use value enabled to enable (true)/disable (false) segment

  • pixelTypeRules - Set new rules for segment membership definition. Applicable only to segment of type "PIXEL"

  • clickersCampaigns - Set a new list of campaign ids for segment membership definition. Applicable only to segment of type "CLICKERS"

  • membershipDuration - Set a new membership duration

  • clearTrackingStatus - Reset segment tracking

  • archived - Use value archived to archive (true) segment. Archived segments are returned by the segments APIs only where request parameter "includeArchived" is permitted and set to "true"

  • lookalikeSettings - Set new settings of a LOOK_A_LIKES segment |

resources.description:
The Segment object has the following attributes:

Property Type Semantic Example Comments
id String segment id. read-only "00f4b02153ee75f3c9dc4fc128ab041962"
name String segment name. "My Segment"
description String segment description. "all clicks which originated from..."
marketerId String marketer id. read-only "00f4b02153ee75f3c9dc4fc128ab041971"
segmentType SegmentType the type of the segment. read-only
pixelTypeRules PixelTypeRules an object describing rules defining membership to PIXEL segment. only applicable to segments of type PIXEL
conversion SegmentConversion an object describing the conversion the segment is based on. For segment type VALUABLE_CONVERSION contains also the rule that defines membership to Value Based Converters segment. only applicable to segments of type CONVERSION or VALUABLE_CONVERSION
clickersCampaigns Array of String a collection of campaign ids defining membership to CLICKERS segment only applicable to segments of type CLICKERS
enabled Boolean is the segment enabled.
membershipDuration Integer number of days a user should be attributed to a segment.
trackingStatus TrackingStatus indicates if the segment is active/inactive. The status will be "inactive" until the first user has been added to the cookie pool, once a user has been added the status will be “active” indicating the pixel is firing and collecting new users. read-only "INACTIVE" only applicable to segments of type PIXEL. Can only receive the value "true".
archived Boolean indicates if the segment is archived/un-archived.

actions.name: Create a PromotedLink
actions.description:
You can create a new promoted link and associate it with an existing campaign. AmplifyAPi allows you to add your own headline, image and section name for the newly created promoted link. If you'd like to set your own image, then you can do so by providing an http link for the hosted image or by uploadig an image file. if the image is not provided, it will be set via our backend crawler.

POST a JSON hash with the following attributes:

  • text - optional, if not provided, the title will be set via our backend crawler. NOTE: Outbrain supports the ability to include dynamic values in the headline (English-only) for location and day of week. For more information and instructions on the proper syntax please visit: https://www.outbrain.com/help/advertisers/add-content/#dynamic

  • url - mandatory

  • enabled - mandatory

  • cpcAdjustment - optional

  • sectionName - optional

  • description - optional

  • imageMetadata - optional

    • id - optional, Outbrain image id in case the image has already been uploaded
    • url - optional, http link for the hosted image
      • If the image format is mp4, the video should be up to 10sec long
    • playMode - optional, the image Play Mode type. Relevant to MP4 and GIF image types. - Determines whether the clip would run once or loop 3 times.
    • cropSettings - optional, array of Crop Point. Relevant for Standard images only
    • cropType - optional, the image’s custom Crop Type
    • aiGenerated - optional, whether this creative was fully or partially generated or modified by an AI tool

  • logoMetadata - optional, this PromotedLink's own brand logo. If omitted, the advertiser's Marketer.logoMetadata is copied in as a one-time default

    • id - optional, Outbrain logo id if already uploaded
    • url - optional, http link for the hosted logo image

resourceGroups.name: PromotedLinksSequences
resourceGroups.description:
Sequences comes in 2 formats:

  • Carousel - multi-promotedLink format that features CTA buttons, brand logo, and more. You can use Carousel to tell your brand story, showcase multiple products, and build a sequential message — with up to 10 images for consumers to swipe through.

    • In order to create sequences of this type your campaign’s creative format must be Carousel (see Campaign creative format)
    • A carousel must have at least 3 promoted links and up to 10 promoted links in it
    • A campaign can have only 1 carousel
    • Promoted links can’t be duplicated in the same carousel
    • All promoted links must be in the same language
    • App rating us supported only for sequences of type AppInstall

  • App Install - gives you the ability to present your promoted link with logo, sponsor, app rating and direct redirect to google/apple store to download and install the app.

    • In order to create sequences of this type your campaign’s creative format must be AppInstall (see Campaign creative format)
    • An App Install can have 1 promoted link
    • A campaign can have multiple app install sequences
    • Sequence title is not supported

Promoted link sequence object has the following attributes:

sponser String The sponsor’s name “sponser”

appDetails App Details Object
creationTime Date When was the sequence created "2019-05-22 12:23:37"
lastModified Date Last time the sequence was modified "2019-05-23 12:23:37"

resourceGroups.name: Performance Reporting
resourceGroups.description:
There are a multitude of reporting endpoints that allow you to retrieve metrics at various levels of granularity.

Note: All performance reports have a 10-30 minutes delay, therefore performance metrics that include the current day are partial.

Rate Limits

Each marketer is limited to 30 requests per minute for the entire performance reporting API. In case of rate limit violation the response status will be 429 (Too Many Requests).

As of April 12, 2021 performance reporting is limited to a history of 3 years per data request.

Response structure

All reporting endpoints share a common response structure, defined below:

Property Type Semantic Comments
results Array Metadata and Metrics of the entities returned. Metadata is an object containing contextual properties of the report entity. The set of properties is specific for each end-point.
totalResults Number Count of the total results (without filtering).
summary Metrics Total aggregated metrics for the set of data returned in this response (without filtering).
totalFilteredResults Number Count of the total results after filtering. Optional, included for requests with filter parameter.
summaryFiltered Metrics Aggregated metrics for the set of data returned in this response after filtering. Optional, included for requests with filter parameter.

Metrics

Object containing performance metric fields. The spend field and all derived fields are based on the marketer currency, available in each of the marketer's budget object (see Budget).

Property Type Semantic Comments
impressions Number Total number of PromotedLinks impressions across the entire query range.
viewableImpressions Number Total number of ad impressions that met the viewability standard. Optional, included only when includeViewedImpressions is true.
clicks Number Total PromotedLinks clicks across the entire query range.
ctr Number The average CTR (Click Through Rate) percentage across the entire query range (clicks / impressions)/100.
spend Money The total amount of money spent across the entire query range.
ecpc Money (3 digits precision) The effective (calculated) average CPC (Cost Per Click) across the entire query range spend / clicks.
totalConversions Number The total number of conversions calculated across the entire query range. By default conversions are reported by time of conversion, there is an option to report by time of event (click or view) by setting conversionsByClickDate to true.
conversions Number The total number of conversions from clicks calculated across the entire query range. By default conversions are reported by time of conversion, there is an option to report by time of click by setting conversionsByClickDate to true.
viewConversions Number The total number of view-through conversions calculated across the entire query range. By default conversions are reported by time of conversion, there is an option to report by time of view by setting conversionsByClickDate to true.
conversionRate Number The average rate of conversions from clicks per click percentage across the entire query range (conversions / clicks)/100.
viewConversionRate Number The average rate of view-through conversions per viewable impression percentage across the entire query range.
cpa Number The average CPA (Cost Per Acquisition) calculated for conversions from clicks across the entire query range spend / conversions.
totalCpa Number The average CPA (Cost Per Acquisition) calculated for all conversions across the entire query range spend / totalConversions.
totalSumValue Money The total amount of money reported for all conversions for the entire query range.
sumValue Money The total amount of money reported for conversions from clicks for the entire query range.
viewSumValue Money The total amount of money reported for view-through conversions for the entire query range.
totalAverageValue Money The average amount of money reported for all conversions for the entire query range totalSumValue / totalConversions.
averageValue Money The average amount of money reported for conversions from clicks for the entire query range sumValue / conversions.
viewAverageValue Money The average amount of money reported for view-through conversions for the entire query range viewSumValue / viewConversions.
roas Number Return On Ad Spend is your total conversion value attributed to clicks, divided by spend for the entire query range sumValue / spend
totalRoas Number Total Return On Ad Spend is your total conversion value attributed to clicks or views, divided by spend for the entire query range totalSumValue / spend
conversionMetrics ConversionMetrics array Metrics for each conversion pixel for the entire query range Optional, included only when includeConversionDetails is true.
cpm Money Cost per thousand impressions. Calculated by dividing the amount spent by the impressions multiplied by 1000.
dstFeeCost Money The Digital Services Tax (DST) that is added in some of your targeted countries.

Conversion Metrics

Object containing performance metrics for conversion pixels.

Property Type Semantic
name String The conversion pixel name.
totalConversions Number The total number of conversions for the conversion pixel.
conversions Number The total number of conversions from clicks for the conversion pixel.
viewsConversions Number The total number of view-through conversions for the conversion pixel.
conversionRate Number The average rate of conversions from clicks per click percentage for the conversion pixel (conversions / clicks)/100.
viewConversionRate Number The average rate of view-through conversions per viewable impressions percentage for the conversion pixel.
cpa Number The average CPA (Cost Per Acquisition) calculated conversions from clicks for the conversion pixel from clicks spend / conversions.
totalCpa Number The average CPA (Cost Per Acquisition) calculated for the conversion pixel from clicks spend / totalConversions.
totalSumValue Money The total amount of money reported for all conversions for the conversion pixel totalSumValue / totalConversions.
sumValue Money The total amount of money reported for conversions from clicks for the conversion pixel sumValue / conversions.
viewSumValue Money The total amount of money reported for view-through conversions for the conversion pixel viewSumValue / viewConversions.
totalAverageValue Money The average amount of money reported for all conversions for the conversion pixel totalSumValue / totalConversions.
averageValue Money The average amount of money reported for conversions from clicks for the conversion pixel sumValue / conversions.
viewAverageValue Money The average amount of money reported for view-through conversions for the conversion pixel viewSumValue / viewConversions.
roas Number Return On Ad Spend is your total conversion value attributed to clicks, divided by spend for the conversion pixel sumValue / spend.
totalRoas Number Total Return On Ad Spend is your total conversion value attributed to clicks or views, divided by spend for the conversion pixel totalSumValue / spend.

In order to use conversion metric fields in sorting and filtering, the field name should be formatted as follows: conversionMetrics/{conversionField}/{conversionName}, where {conversionField} is the conversion metric field name, and {conversionName} is the conversion pixel name with all spaces replaced by '-'.

For example, the conversionRate field of a conversion pixel with the name "registration" is represented by conversionMetrics/conversionRate/registration. The cpa field of a conversion pixel with the name "full event" is represented by conversionMetrics/cpa/full-event.

Apple SKAdNetwork conversions

Apple SKAdNetwork conversions have limited data and thus will not appear the same as standard Outbrain conversions: All Apple Conversions will be written at the time the data is received from the Apple servers. Apple Conversions will not be included in Conversion totals. This Data is available in Campaign, Month, Date, Day of Week, Publisher and Platform (under Mobile, iOS and in-app by default) reports.

To include Apple SKAdNetwork conversions metrics in the response add the following parameter to your request: includeAppleSkAdNetworkData=true.

The following properties will be added to the response's Metrics object.

Property Type Semantic
appleSKAdNetworkConversions Number The total number of conversions determined by Apple to be attributed to Outbrain.
appleSKAdNetworkRedownload0 Number The number of conversions that are first time downloads as determined by Apple.
appleSKAdNetworkRedownload1 Number The number of conversions that are redownloads, as determined by Apple.
appleSKAdNetworkConversionValue Number Aggregate of the value passed for all conversions as determined by Apple.
appleSKAdNetworkConversionAverageValue Number The average of the conversion value passed from Apple.

Video (click-to-watch) metrics

Video metrics are not available for Interest report.

Note: The general measure of clicks for a click-to-watch campaign indicates the number of unique video plays across the requested date range. This measure should not be confused with clicksOnVideo which indicates clicks happening after the video started playing.

To include video metrics in the response add the following parameter to your request: includeVideoStats=true.

The following properties will be added to the response's Metrics object.

Property Type Semantic
videoReachedFirstQ Number Indicates the number of views reaching 25% point in videos timeline.
videoReachedSecondQ Number Indicates the number of views reaching 50% point in videos timeline.
videoReachedThirdQ Number Indicates the number of views reaching 75% point in videos timeline.
videoReachedCompletion Number Indicates the number of fully viewed videos.
videoAvgViewDuration Seconds Indicates the average time users spend watching the video.
clicksOnVideo Number Indicates the number of clicks on the video or on the CTA button during the playtime.
videoActiveCompletions Number Indicates the number of user actions representing active completion (redirections or completions).
videoActiveCompletionsPercentage Number Indicates the percentage of user actions representing active completion (redirections or completions) out of the total plays.
videoPlays Number The number of all video plays (non unique).

Request Structure

All reporting endpoints share common request parameters, defined below:

Parameter Type Semantic Details
from String First date in requested date range, format "YYYY-MM-DD" Required
to String Last date in requested date range, format "YYYY-MM-DD" Required
limit Number Maximal number of results to return. Optional, default 10, maximal value 500
offset Number The first result to return (number of results to skip). Optional, default 0
sort Object Set the sorting order of results, defined below. Optional
filter Object Set filtering of results, defined below. Optional
includeArchivedCampaigns Boolean Include or ignore results from archived campaigns Optional, default false
budgetId String Limit to data of the budget with given ID Optional
campaignId String Limit to data of the campaign with given ID Optional, takes precedence over budgetId
includeConversionDetails Boolean Include or exclude conversion pixels metrics Optional, default false
conversionsByClickDate Boolean Conversion metrics reported by click date (true) or by conversion date (false) Optional, default false

Sort Parameters

The sort parameter contains a sort direction charachter, '+' for ascending and '-' for descending, followed by the name of the performance or metadata field to sort by. The list of specific fields relevant for each endpoint is given in its definition.

For example, '-spend' will sort results by spend value descending.

Filter Parameters

The following table describes the basic filter operators. The first example will filter campaigns leaving only those whose name is 'Campaign X'.

Operator Description Example
eq Equal /campaigns?filter=name eq 'Campaign X'
ne Not equal /budgets?filter=name ne 'Budget Y'
gt Greater than /publishers?filter=spend gt 20
ge Greater than or equal /sections?filter=clicks ge 10
lt Less than /campaigns?filter=conversions lt 20
le Less than or equal /content?filter=ctr le 0.1
and Logical and /campaigns?filter=spend gt 20 and clicks ge 10
or Logical or /sections?filter=conversions lt 20 or ctr le 0.1
not Logical negation /publishers?filter=not ecpc gt 1.0

You can chain filters with the and or or operators, for example clicks+gt+99+and+cpc+lt+0.7.

Nesting of Boolean operators is not supported currently.

The following table describes string comparison functions available in filtering. The first example will filter campaigns leaving only those whose name contains the string 'USA'.

Function Example Comments
substringof(searchInString, searchString) substringof(name,'USA') Name of filtered field given in 'searchInString'. Case insensitive.
startswith(searchInString, prefixString) startswith(name,'Desktop') Name of filtered field given in 'searchInString'. Case insensitive.

resources.description:
The API in this sub-section allows retrieving marketer campaigns data with performance statistics.

Result fields

Metrics in metrics, metadata in a metadata object containing the following fields:

Property Type Semantic
id String Campaign ID.
name String Campaign name.
campaignOnAir Boolean Is the campaign on air, same as campaignOnAir in Live Status.
onAirReason Campaign On Air Reason The reason for the campaign on air status, same as onAirReason in Live Status.
enabled Boolean Is the campaign enabled.
budget Budget Partial Budget entity of a campaign. For full details use Budget.
lastCappingTime Time Optional. Latest date and time the campaign was capped for selected date range. Data is available for up to 30 days ago.
cpc Money Cost per monetized user action (for example cost per click). See Currencies for valid cost values.
creativeFormat Campaign creative format The campaign creative format.

resources.name: Promoted Content

actions.name: Retrieve promoted content links performance statistics for a Marketer

parameters.description: Marketer id
Start day Date
End day Date
Number of results to return in this request. Used with offset for pagination. default is 10.

Include data of archived campaigns, default false.
Limit to data of the budget with the given ID.
Limit to data of the campaign with the given IDs (takes precedence over budgetId).
Limit to data of the promoted link with the given ID (takes precedence over budgetId and campaignId).
Limit to data of the promoted sequence link with the given ID (takes precedence over budgetId and campaignId).
Include metrics of conversion pixels, default false.
Report conversion metrics by click or conversion date, default false (report by conversion date).
Include data of active campaigns only (data of inactive campaigns will not be shown). Relevant only when requesting all campaigns

resources.description:
The API in this sub-section allows retrieving performance statistics by promoted link at different levels: marketer, budget, campaign and promoted link.

This new endpoint also supports promoted links that are creative format: CAROUSEL and APP_INSTALL, these were previously excluded from the original Content endpoint. Please note that this endpoint is replacing the previous Content endpoint which will be removed by October 2022.

Result fields

Metrics in metrics, metadata in a metadata object containing the following fields:

Property Type Semantic
id String The ID of the PromotedLink.
sequenceId String The ID of the PromotedLinkSequence.
title String The title of the PromotedLink.
creationTime Date The time when the PromotedLink was created.
lastModified Date The time when the PromotedLink was last modified.
url String The URL visitors will be sent to upon clicking the PromotedLink.
status PromotedLink Review Status Deprecated, use approvalStatus instead. The review status of the PromotedLink.
approvalStatus PromotedLink Approval Status The approval status of the PromotedLink.
enabled Boolean Will this PromotedLink be served.
cachedLogoUrl String The URL of the PromotedLink's logo image, cached on Outbrain's servers.
campaignId String The ID of the campaign to which the PromotedLink belongs.
campaignName String The name of the campaign to which the PromotedLink belongs.
sectionName String The section name of the site the PromotedLink URL points to.
cpcAdjustment Number CPC adjustment bid of this PromotedLink for campaign given by the campaignId parameter (optional).
creativeFormat Campaign creative format The creative format of the campaign to which the PromotedLink belongs to.
imageMetadata Image Meta Data PromotedLink's image metadata
metadata String non-serving reference name of the PromotedLink (optional)

Special request parameters

Parameter Type Semantic Details
promotedLinkId String Limit to data of the promoted link with given ID Optional, takes precedence over budgetId and campaignId
sequenceId String Limit to data of the promoted link sequence with given ID Optional, takes precedence over budgetId and campaignId
limit Number Maximal number of results to return. Optional, default 10, maximal value 1000

resources.description:
The API in this sub-section allows retrieving performance statistics by periodic breakdown at different levels: marketer, budget, campaign and promoted link.

Special request parameters

Parameter Type Semantic Details
breakdown String Defines the periodic breakdown of data, either daily, weekly, monthly, hourOfDay, dayOfWeek or dayOfWeekByHour. Optional, default value daily.
promotedLinkId String Limit to data of the promoted link with given ID. Optional, takes precedence over budgetId and campaignId. Not allowed with hourOfDay or dayOfWeekByHour breakdown.

Result fields

Metrics in metrics, metadata in a metadata object containing the following fields:

Property Type Supported Breakdowns Semantic
id String All date range identifier (month in format 'yyyy-MM' or start date in format 'yyyy-MM-dd', or day of week and hour in format 'd-HH')
fromDate Date daily, weekly, monthly The first day of the result date period.
toDate Date daily, weekly, monthly The last day of the result date period (inclusive).
lastCappingTime Time portion of Time, in format "HH:mm:ss". daily for a single campaign. Optional. The time the campaign was capped during that date. Data is available for up to 30 days ago.
hourOfDay String hourOfDay, dayOfWeekByHour The day of the week (Monday, Tuesday, etc.) of the result period.
dayOfWeek Hour Of Day dayOfWeek, dayOfWeekByHour The hour of day of the result period.
cpcAdjustment Number dayOfWeekByHour CPC adjustment bid of this day and hour for campaign given by the campaignId parameter (optional).
enabled Boolean dayOfWeekByHour The scheduling status of this day and hour for campaign given by the campaignId parameter (optional).

Note: The response structure defers from other performance responses.

promotedLinkResults Array Results for the campaign promoted links. Each object in the array contains results and totalResults field similar to the response of the Periodic request, and an additional promotedLinkId field with the campaign ID.
totalPromotedLinks Number Count of the total promoted links in the promotedLinkResults array.

blockStatus Block status Blocking status of the publisher.
blockTypes Block types Block types and their value for the publisher.
url String Publisher's site URL (optional).
isOen Boolean Is this an OEN (Outbrain Extended Network) publisher. (Planned removal October 18th)

resources.description:
A special endpoint for retrieving publishers data by campaign breakdown.

Note: The response structure defers from other performance responses.

The reponse contains only campaigns that have publishers results given the offset and limit, in the following two objects:

Property Type Semantic
campaignResults Array Results for the marketer campaigns. Each object in the array contains results and totalResults field similar to the response of the Publishers request (except for the blockStatus and blockTypes fields in the metadata field of each result), and an additional campaignId field with the campaign ID.
totalCampaigns Number Count of the total campaigns in the campaignResults array.

parameters.description: Marketer id
Start day Date
End day Date
Number of results to return in this request. Used with offset for pagination. default is 10.
Result number to start this response at. zero based. Used with limit for pagination. default is 0.
Can have one of the following values impressions, clicks, ctr, spend, ecpc, conversions, conversionRate, cpa, publisherName, name. For more details about reports filtering read this.
Can have the following values impressions, clicks, ctr, spend, ecpc, conversions, conversionRate, cpa, publisherId, publisherName, name. For more details about reports filtering read this.
Include data of archived campaigns, default false.
Limit to data of the budget with the given ID.
Limit to data of the campaign with the given IDs (takes precedence over budgetId).
Include metrics of conversion pixels, default false.
Report conversion metrics by click or conversion date, default false (report by conversion date).
When true, includes viewableImpressions in the response metrics.
Include data of active campaigns only (data of inactive campaigns will not be shown). Relevant only when requesting all campaigns

resources.description:
Section: A specific content section within the publisher's site such as sports, business etc.

The API in this sub-section allows retrieving marketer performance statistics with breakdown by section with sections that are already blocked at the marketer or campaign level.

Note: Sections with less than 1 click or less than 10 impressions will not show up in the results.

Result Fields

Metrics in metrics, metadata in a metadata object containing the following fields:

Property Type Semantic
id String Section Identifier.
name String Section Name.
publisherId String Identifiers of the publisher related to the section.
publisherName String Name of the publisher related to the section.
cpcAdjustment Number CPC adjustment bid of this section for campaign given by the campaignId parameter (optional).
blockStatus Block status Blocking status of the section.
blockTypes Block types Block types and their value for the section.
publisherUrl String URL of this section's publisher (optional).
isOen Boolean Is this an OEN (Outbrain Extended Network) section. (Planned removal October 18th)

resources.description:
A special endpoint for retrieving sections data by campaign breakdown.

Note: The response structure defers from other performance responses.

Note 2: Sections with less than 1 click or less than 10 impressions will not show up in the results.

The reponse contains only campaigns that have sections results given the offset and limit, in the following two objects:

Property Type Semantic
campaignResults Array Results for the marketer campaigns. Each object in the array contains results and totalResults field similar to the response of the Sections request (except for the cpcAdjustment, blockStatus and blockTypes fields in the metadata field of each result), and an additional campaignId field with the campaign ID.
totalCampaigns Number Count of the total campaigns in the campaignResults array.

resources.name: Sections by date

actions.name: Retrieve performance statistics for all marketer sections by dates

parameters.description: Marketer id
Start day Date
End day Date
Limit to data of the campaign with the given IDs.
Number of results to return in this request for each date. default is 10.
Result number to start this response at. zero based. Used with limit for pagination. default is 0.
Include data of archived campaigns, default false.
Include metrics of conversion pixels, default false.
Report conversion metrics by click or conversion date, default false (report by conversion date).
Include data of active campaigns only (data of inactive campaigns will not be shown). Relevant only when requesting all campaigns

total Number Count of the total sections in the results array. The returned values will be only the paginated data according the the offset and limit inputs.

resources.description:
The API in this sub-section allows retrieving performance statistics by interest at different levels: marketer and campaign.

In all other performance reporting endpoints each user action (impression, click or conversion) is attributed to a single entity, for example campaign, section or region.

Interests behave differently, since users can have multiple interests in their Outbrain Interest Profile and therefore data repeats between interests. For example, a user may be interested in both health and politics and so an impression, click or conversion will be attributed to both interests. As a result, the sum of the total interests reported does not represent the actual sum of action taken.

Therefore, the summary and summaryFiltered metrics are not included in the response of interest performance reports.

Result fields

Metrics in metrics, metadata in a metadata object containing the following fields:

Property Type Semantic
id String Interest id.
name String The name of the interest. Interests with hierarchy are given with a '>' symbol separating the interests level, for example 'News > Weather'.
targetingStatus String The targeting status of the interest, one of targeted, excluded, notTargeted, partiallyTargeted or partiallyExcluded.

resourceGroups.name: Reference Types
resourceGroups.description:
Date

All date attributes are in 'yyyy-MM-dd' format. E.g. January 11th, 2015 is: 2015-01-26.

Time

All time attributes are in 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss' format, where the time is with accordance to ET with 0..23 hour representation. E.g. 2013-02-28 17:43:19.

Hour of Day

All hour of day attributes are in 'HH:00' format. E.g. 4pm is: 16:00 while 4am is: 04:00

Money

Money is a decimal number with precision of 2 digits after the decimal point.

Platform

A platform is one of the following:

  • DESKTOP - The content was consumed via desktop.

  • MOBILE - The content was consumed via mobile.

  • TABLET - The content was consumed via tablet.

Platform Operating System

A platform breakdown operating system can be one of the following:

  • Ios - The content was consumed via Ios.

  • MacOs - The content was consumed via MacOs.

  • Android - The content was consumed via Android.

  • Windows - The content was consumed via Windows.

  • Other - The content was consumed via Other operating system.

Platform Browser

A platform breakdown browser can be one of the following:

  • Chrome - The content was consumed via Chrome browser.

  • Firefox - The content was consumed via Firefox browser.

  • Safari - The content was consumed via Safari browser.

  • InternetExplorer - The content was consumed via InternetExplorer browser.

  • Opera - The content was consumed via Opera browser.

  • Samsung - The content was consumed via Samsung browser.

  • UCBrowser - The content was consumed via UCBrowser.

  • InApp - The content was consumed via InApp browser.

  • Edge - The content was consumed via Edge browser. Data only available as separate from Internet explorer starting on July 13th, 2020.

  • Other - The content was consumed via Other browser.

Review Status

A PromotedLink review status is one of the following:

  • APPROVED - PromotedLink content is approved

  • PENDING - PromotedLink content is in the proccess of being reviewed

  • REJECTED - PromotedLink content is rejected

Approval Review Status

A PromotedLink approval status is one of the following:

  • Approved - PromotedLink content is approved

  • Pending - PromotedLink content is in the proccess of being reviewed

  • Rejected - PromotedLink content is rejected

Approval Status

A PromotedLink Approval Status Object has the following attributes:

Property Type Semantic
status ApprovalReviewStatus The Status of the PromotedLink) read only
reasons array of String (Optional) Indicates the reasons only if your content is rejected (ApprovalReviewStatus is Rejected) read only
isEditable Boolean Indicates if the PromotedLink is able to be edited. true if the ApprovalReviewStatus is Pending)

OnAir Status

A PromotedLink OnAir Status Object has the following attributes:

Property Type Semantic
onAir Boolean Indicates whether the PromotedLinks is onAir (can be served) read only
reason String (Optional) Indicates a meaningful reason in case the onAir property is false read only

Campaign On Air Reason

A Campaign on air reason is one of the following:

  • CAMPAIGN_ON_AIR

  • CAMPAIGN_DISABLED - Your campaign is Paused. Switch to play to run it.

  • CAMPAIGN_FLY_DATES_PAST - Your campaign has ended.

  • CAMPAIGN_FLY_DATES_FUTURE - Your campaign is scheduled to start on a future date.

  • CAMPAIGN_DAILY_CAPPED - Your daily budget has been reached and will resume tomorrow. To increase running time, edit budget settings.

  • CAMPAIGN_DAILY_CAPPED_MONTHLY - Your budget for the day has been reached. Your campaign will resume tomorrow, and has used <CURRENCY_SYMBOL><spentAmount> of its monthly budget.

  • CAMPAIGN_DAILY_CAPPED_CAMPAIGN - Your budget for the day has been reached. Your campaign will resume tomorrow, and has used <CURRENCY_SYMBOL><spentAmount> of its budget.

  • CAMPAIGN_BUDGET_DEPLETED - Your campaign has reached its monthly budget limit, and will resume on the first day of next month.

  • CAMPAIGN_ALL_PROMOTED_LINKS_DISABLED - Your content is not enabled.

  • CAMPAIGN_ALL_PROMOTED_LINKS_REJECTED - Your content has not been approved. View content guidelines.

  • ALL_PROMOTED_LINKS_EXPIRED - Your content has expired.

  • ALL_PROMOTED_LINKS_PENDING - Your content is under editorial review.

  • WAITING_FOR_START_HOUR - Your campaign will resume at its scheduled start time tomorrow.

  • NO_RUNNING_PROMOTED_LINKS - Your content is not currently running.

  • MISSING_BILLING_INFO - There is no credit card on file for this account. Please contact us.

  • EXPIRED_BILLING_INFO - The credit card on file expired. Please contact us.

  • FAILED_BILLING_INFO - There is a problem with the credit card on file. Please contact us.

  • BAD_CONTENT - The account is blocked. For more details please contact us.

  • OUTSTANDING_UNPAID_BALANCE - There is outstanding balance on the account. Please contact us.

  • TOS_VIOLATION - There is a problem with the account. Please contact us.

  • NEW_CUSTOMER_PENDING - Your content is under review. Please contact uswith any questions.

  • PAUSED - There is a problem with the account. Please contact us.

  • MARKED_DELETED - This account is no longer active. To resume please contact us.

  • LEGACY_UNKNOWN - There is a problem with the account. Please contact us.

  • FAILED_THRESHOLD_BILLING - There is a problem with the credit card on file. Please contact us.

  • CAMPAIGN_NOT_IN_SCHEDULING_HOURS - Your campaign will resume according to it's scheduling configuration.

  • ALL_DOCUMENTS_UNAVAILABLE - All of your campaign content links currently cannot be reached.

Call To Action

A PromotedLink Call To Action Object has the following attributes:

Property Type Semantic
type Call To Action Type Indicates call to action type on promoted link
value String Call to action type translation read only

Call To Action Type

Call to action type is one of the following:

  • NONE

  • APPLY_NOW

  • BOOK_NOW

  • CONTACT_US

  • DOWNLOAD

  • LEARN_MORE

  • GET_QUOTE

  • SHOP_NOW

  • SIGN_UP

  • WATCH_MORE

  • LISTEN_NOW

  • SUBSCRIBE

  • RSVP

  • REGISTER_NOW

  • INSTALL_APP

  • READ_MORE

  • PLAY_GAME

  • DONATE_NOW

Image Meta Data

A PromotedLink's image metadata:

Property Type Semantic
id String Unique image identifier. On input, use instead of url to reuse an already-uploaded image. (optional)
url String On input, an http link to the image to use, no separate upload needed. (input only, optional)
requestedImageUrl String The image url with the requested dimensions. (output only)
originalImageUrl String The image url with the original dimensions. output only. optional
thumbnailUrl String The image thumbnail url for MP4/GIF image type. output only
playMode Play Mode type The image play mode type (relevant to MP4 and GIF image types) - Determines whether the clip would run once or loop 3 times.
stream String The image content in bytes. input only. optional
type Image type The image type. output only
cropSettings array of Crop Point The image custom crop settings. can be sent only for Standard images. optional
cropType Crop Type The image’s custom crop type. (optional)
aiGenerated Boolean Whether this creative was fully or partially generated or modified by an AI tool. When true, Teads embeds a compliant AI watermark with correctly encoded C2PA metadata before delivery. When false or omitted, you confirm the creative is either non-AI, or already carries compliant AI watermarks and metadata — in which case Teads preserves them as supplied and you retain responsibility for their accuracy. Accurate declaration is required under EU AI Act Article 50(4), applicable from 2 August 2026. False or missing declarations may result in creative rejection, account suspension, and regulatory penalties.

Provide at most one of id or url.

Logo Meta Data

A Marketer's brand logo metadata:

Property Type Semantic
url String The logo image url. Typically the only field you need, Outbrain fetches and stores the image for you. (optional)
id String Logo id, echoed back on output. Rarely needed on input, only to re-apply a previously-returned logo. (optional)

Provide at most one of id or url.

Play Mode Type

An Image Play Mode type is one of the following:

  • Once

  • Loop

Image Type

An Image type is one of the following:

  • Standard

  • GIF

  • MP4

Crop Point

A Crop Point consist from:

Property Type Semantic
ratio Ratio type Image Ratio
x Integer Image top left x coordinate
y Integer Image top left y coordinate
w Integer Image custom width
h Integer Image custom height

Crop Point Ratio Type

A Ratio type is one of the following:

  • 1:1

  • 4:3

  • 3:2

  • 8:5

  • 16:9

  • 1.91:1

Crop Type

An Image Crop type is one of the following:

  • Fill

  • Blur

  • DominantColor

Budget Type

A Budget type is one of the following:

  • CAMPAIGN - The budget is one-time and does not repeat

  • MONTHLY - The budget repeats per month

  • DAILY - The budget repeats per day

Pacing Type

A pacing type is one of the following:

  • SPEND_ASAP - The budget should be spent ASAP, with no daily capping

  • AUTOMATIC - Allow the Outbrain engine to decide on the budget spend pacing

  • DAILY_TARGET - The budget should be spent on a daily basis, with a limit at this target amount

Campaign Optimization Type

Represents the type of the campaign optimization.

  • TRAFFIC - Campaign optimized towards maximizing traffic (clicks)

  • CPC - Campaign optimized towards bringing traffic to the highest converting sections using automatic CPC adjustment per serving

  • MAX_CONVERSION_FULLY_AUTOMATED - Campaign optimized towards maximizing the number of conversions within your budget. Note: this mode might change your campaign’s CPC.

  • TARGET_CPA_FULLY_AUTOMATED - Campaign optimized towards a target CPA for a specific conversion event. Note: this mode might change your campaign’s CPC.

  • TARGET_ROAS_FULLY_AUTOMATED - Campaign optimized towards a target ROAS for a specific conversion event. Note: this mode might change your campaign’s CPC. Click here to learn more about target ROAS.

Max Daily Average CPC Recommendation

In case your CBS automatic campaign can not increase the CPC (and the algorithm recommends to increase it), follow these recommendations

  • INCREASE_BID_CAP - Increase the value of automaticModeMaxAvgDailyCpc (or for old campaigns - automaticModeMaxCpc)

  • INCREASE_TARGET_CPA - There is no automaticModeMaxAvgDailyCpc, but your target CPA is lower than the desired CPC. Increase the target CPA

  • NO_RECOMMENDATION_INTERNAL_ERROR - an error occured during recommendation calculation

  • NO_RECOMMENDATION_MAX_CURRENCY - there is no recommendation

Volume Control Adjustment Level

Represents the desired volume adjustment for a section.

  • INCREASE - Significantly increase traffic from the section.

  • SLIGHTLY_INCREASE - Slightly increase traffic from the section.

  • SLIGHTLY_DECREASE - Slightly decrease traffic from the section.

Campaign On Air Type

Represents the scheduling type for the campaign to be on air.

  • Scheduled - Campaign will be on air based on it's Scheduling Rules.

  • StartHour - Campaign will be on air based on it's StartHour property.

Day Of Week

  • Sunday

  • Monday

  • Tuesday

  • Wednesday

  • Thursday

  • Friday

  • Saturday

Content Type

A content type is one of the following:

  • ARTICLES - The content of this campaign is articles

  • NATIVE_VIDEO - The content of this campaign is video

Segment Type

A segment type is one of the following:

  • PIXEL - This segment type includes users who visited a specific page on your site (membership defined by a set of pixel rules)

  • CLICKERS - This segment type includes users who clicked on a specific campaign (membership defined by a list of clicker campaigns)

  • DMP - This segment type includes the users from your specific DMP segment.

  • LOOK_A_LIKES - This segment type includes similar users from your seed segment. You can create lookalike based of the following segment types: CLICKERS, PIXEL and DMP.

  • CONVERSION - This segment type includes users which are candidates for conversion.

  • VALUABLE_CONVERSION - This segment type includes users that triggered a conversion that is worth a defined value (based on the defined rule).

Pixel Rule Type

A pixel rule type is one of the following:

  • UrlStartsWith - The rule enforces a match on the url prefix

  • UrlDoesNotStartWith - The rule enforces a lack of match on the url prefix

  • UrlEndsWith - The rule enforces a match the url suffix

  • UrlDoesNotEndWith - The rule enforces a lack of match the url suffix

  • UrlContains - The rule enforces a match on a substring of the url

  • UrlDoesNotContain - The rule enforces a lack of match on a substring of the url

  • UrlEquals - The rule enforces a match to the entire url

  • UrlDoesNotEqual - The rule enforces a lack of match on the url prefix

Value Based Converters Rule Type

A Value Based Converters rule type is one of the following:

  • EqualsTo - The rule enforces a match on the value of conversion

  • GreaterThanEqual - The rule enforces a match or a greater number on the value of converesion

  • LowerThan - The rule enforces a lower number on the value of the conversion

  • BetweenInclusive - The rule enforces an inclusive range on the value of the conversion

Tracking Status

A tracking status is one of the following. The status will be "inactive" until the first user has been added to the cookie pool, once a user has been added the status will be “active” indicating the pixel is firing and collecting new users.

  • ACTIVE - The tracking status is active

  • INACTIVE - The tracking status is inactive

Block status

The blocking status of a publisher or section. Can be one of the following:

  • Unblocked - No blocking at any level

  • Blocked - Fully blocked at all levels

  • PartialBlock - Blocking on some levels

Block types

A map of block types to Boolean values, describing the blocking status (true for blocked, false for non-blocked) of a publisher or section in context of entire marketer or specific campaign. Map key values:

  • marketerPublisher

  • marketerSection

  • campaignPublisher

  • campaignSection

  • oenOptOut (Planned removal October 18th)

Conversion Event Category

Represents the category of the Conversion Event.

  • CHECKOUT

  • REGISTRATION

  • EMAIL_SIGN_UP

  • VIDEO_VIEW

  • LEAD

  • ADD_TO_CART

  • CONTENT_VIEW

  • DOWNLOAD

  • OTHER

  • SEARCH

  • PURCHASE

  • TIME_ON_PAGE (relevant to engagement conversions only)

  • MOUSE_CLICK (relevant to engagement conversions only)

  • SCROLL_DEPTH (relevant to engagement conversions only)

Conversion Event Type

Represents the type of the Conversion Event.

  • URL_BASED

  • EVENT_BASED

  • ENGAGEMENT

Conversion Event Segment

A Conversion Event Segment Object has the following attributes:

Property Type Semantic
id String The id of the segment read only
name String The name of the segment read only
enabled boolean The segment enabled status read only

Prefix Tracking Code

A Prefix Tracking Code Object has the following attributes:

Property Type Semantic Example Semantic
prefix String The marketer's prefix url "http://www.marketersServer.com?redirectTo="
encode boolean Whether to encode the PromotedLink followed by the prefix or not false true by default.

The prefix property can't contain dynamic parameters.

Suffix Tracking Code

A Suffix Tracking Code is a parameter list that will be appended to the Campaign's PromotedLink. Use the value "EMPTY_SUFFIX" to delete.

A Suffix Tracking Code Object can also contain the following Dynamic Parameters:

  • promoted_link_id - The id of the promoted link

CPC Adjustments

CPC Adjustments allows you to maximize your exposure on specific entities (e.g - publisher sections, promoted links etc.).

With custom CPC adjustments you choose a percentage higher or lower than the fixed campaign CPC based on the entity's performance.

The cpc adjustment calculation is: < cpc > + [< cpc > * < cpc adjustment >]

For example when the campaign's cpc is 0.4 and the cpc adjustment is 0.5, the cpc for the selected entity will be 0.4 + (0.4 * 0.5) = 0.6 and when passing -0.5 0.4 + (0.4 * (-0.5)) = 0.2

In case a cpcAdjustment of an entity is applied together with another entity's cpcAdjustment, The cpc adjustment calculation is: < Campaign’s cpc > + [< cpc > * < entity 1 cpc adjustment > * < entity 2 cpc adjustment > * < by hour cpc adjustment >] For example, in case a cpcAdjustment of a promotedLink is applied together with a section’s cpcAdjustment, The cpc adjustment calculation is: < Campaign’s cpc > + [< cpc > * < promotedLink cpc adjustment > * < section cpc adjustment >

  • CPC adjustments will override any Optimization done on the entity except for day and hour bid adjustment.

  • CPC adjustments are supported only for campaign with optimizationType of CPC and Traffic In case the optimizationType is MAX_CONVERSION_FULLY_AUTOMATED, 'TARGET_ROAS_FULLY_AUTOMATED' or 'TARGET_CPA_FULLY_AUTOMATED', setting or adjusting CPC adjustments will result in an error.

  • Bid adjustments are kept when switching between optimizationType of type CPC or TRAFFIC to MAX_CONVERSION_FULLY_AUTOMATED or 'TARGET_CPA_FULLY_AUTOMATED'. E.g - in case optimizationType is CPC or TRAFFIC, switching to MAX_CONVERSION_FULLY_AUTOMATED, 'TARGET_ROAS_FULLY_AUTOMATED' or 'TARGET_CPA_FULLY_AUTOMATED' will result in not returning the adjustments on a GET call. If the optimizationType is then switched back to CPC, the previous adjustments will return on the GET call.

  • The adjusted cpc can only be between the campaign's min and max cpc (when bidding below the campaign's min cpc the cpc will be the campaign's min cpc and the same goes when bidding above the max cpc)

  • It is not recommended to reduce the CPC too significantly. Setting it 5-10% lower than the fixed CPC will ensure attention is driven to the highest performers.

The following rule will change the campaign's cpc according to the cpcAdjustment between Sunday at 03:00 until Tuesday at 01:00

  • Schema

                   "scheduling": {
                 "cpc": [

                     "endDay: : "Tuesday",

                     "endHour": 1,
                     "cpcAdjustment": 0.1

               }

                   "scheduling": {

                     "endDay: : "Sunday",
                     "startHour": 2,

                     "endHour": 2

The following rule means that the campaigns should be on-air between Tuesday at 02:00 until the next Sunday (in the week after) at 06:00.

country String country code of your subseed audience
platform String platform of your subseed audience

DMP Info

DMP Info object contains info about the DMP segment. The DMP Info object has the following attributes:

Property Type Semantic
provider Provider DMP provider
cost Money additional cost per click in dollar

Interest Targeting

Interest Targeting gives you the abillity to select your preferred interests categories in your campaign setup. Then, using our powerful interest insights and predictive technology, we’ll match you with audiences we know are interested in your desired categories and will surface your content to the people who are most likely to take action.

Interest Targeting Object

The interests property gives you the abillity to configure your desired interests using logical operations:

Basic Interest Term Configuration:

A Basic Term has the following properties:

Property Type Semantic
op And / Or / Not The desired Operation.
ids array of Strings The actual interest ids (can be obtained from the search interests by term or get all available interests inventory end-points).

Advanced Interest Term Configuration:

An Advanced Term has the following properties:

Property Type Semantic
op And / Or / Not The desired Operation.
terms A list of Basic or Advanced Terms.

Interests usage example:

  • Basic Interest Term

                   "interests": {
                    "op":"Or",
                    "ids":["007a3a7bcac3d8414f5e22e5f6512bac62", "002f4e9538befa0a97db5cf3bddb0fc2cd"]
               }

  • Advanced Interest Term ( And of Or's )

                            "interests": {
        "op":"And",
        "terms":[
            {
                "op":"Or",
                "ids":["007a3a7bcac3d8414f5e22e5f6512bac62"]
            },{
                "op":"Or",
                "ids":["002f4e9538befa0a97db5cf3bddb0fc2cd"]
            }
        ]
   }

  • Advanced Interest Term ( Not usage )

           "interests": {
        "op":"Not",
        "terms":[
                  {
                    "op":"Or",
                    "ids":["007a3a7bcac3d8414f5e22e5f6512bac62"]
                  }
        ]
   }

IABCategories Targeting

IABCategories Targeting gives you the abillity to select your preferred IAB categories in your campaign setup.

IABCategories Targeting Object

The same structure as Interest Targeting Object Interest Targeting, The tag is "iabCategories" instead of "interests" and the values are the IAB category ids instead of the interest ids.

IABCategories usage example:

  • IABCategories Term

           "iabCategories": {
          "op": "And",
          "terms": [
            {
              "op": "Not",
              "terms": [
                {
                  "op": "Or",
                  "ids": ["IAB12-1"]
                }
              ]
            },
            {
              "op": "Or",
              "ids": ["IAB12-3"]
            }
          ]
        }

Network

Used to Target MSN publishers only.

Network Object

A network has the following properties:

Property Type Semantic
type String network type, currently the only possible value is PublisherList
selection array of Strings MSN publishers list id 005989514658fab332ace27125dc90eb0c

To target MSN publishers only, use the json below:

"network": {

"type":"PublisherList",

"selection":["005989514658fab332ace27125dc90eb0c"]

}

To stop targeting MSN publishers only, use the json below:

"network": {

"type":"PublisherList",

"selection":[]

}

Segment Availability

Segment Availability object contains info about the availability of the segment.

Property Type Semantic
status String ACTIVE
INACTIVE
DISABLED
inactiveReason String Possible INACTIVE reason values:
- Waiting for pixel - inactive until first pixel received which matches segment's rule
- Pending - inactive until first click received for clickers segment
- Segment size exceeded - segment size exceeded its size limit. New users will not be added
- Segment not in use - segment is not is use by any campaign. New users will not be added
